race_context: The office is the board of Madison-Grant United School Corporation, headquartered near Fairmount (11580 S. E 00 W) and serving parts of Grant and Madison counties, including Fairmount and Summitville {mg_board}{hb_summitville}. State enrollment counts rose from 1,073 students in 2020-21 to 1,987 in 2023-24, 2,024 in 2024-25 and 2,110 in 2025-26 {idoe_enroll}. The district also runs virtual programs with Accel Online (Virtual Preparatory Academy of Indiana and Beacon Academy); in April 2026 the VPREP principal told the board 500 students were already scheduled for 2026-27 and about 150 would graduate that spring {mg_min_20260414}. Superintendent Ben Mann told the board that enrollment fell by 135 students from 2020 to 2025 and by 333 from 2015 to 2025, with graduating classes of 85 to 90 being replaced by kindergarten classes of about 55 {ct_kids}. This guide did not confirm whether the state counts include the virtual students.

Superintendent: Ben Mann, who joined the district in 2016 and has been high school principal and chief financial officer, was named interim superintendent on Jan. 20, 2026 and permanent superintendent on May 26, 2026; he also remains CFO {ct_mann_interim}{ct_mann_perm}. He replaced Steve Vore, who resigned effective Jan. 31, 2026 after 2.5 years as superintendent to take a superintendent job outside Grant County {ct_vore}.

Board: seven members. In 2026 Amanda Kelich is president, Dr. Katti Sneed vice president, David Whybrew secretary and John Hanes assistant secretary; the other members are Wendy Longacre, Bruce Stanley and Lisa Martin {mg_board}{ct_vore}. Members are elected by district (Districts 2, 3 and 7 are labeled 'Grant & Madison' on the state list and District 4 'Madison') {in_list}{gc_cand}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: four seats, one each in Districts 2, 3, 4 and 7, each 'vote for one,' matching the state list {in_list}{gc_cand}{ct_contested}. The Herald Bulletin listed the four incumbents whose seats are up as John Hanes, Katti Sneed, Donald Bruce Stanley and Wendy Longacre {hb_oneweek}. Hanes (District 2) and Stanley (District 4) are unopposed; Sneed faces Dylan C. Vetor in District 3, the only contested race; Erik Davidson is the only District 7 candidate, and Longacre is not on the ballot {gc_cand}{ct_contested}.

Party labels: 2026 is the first election in which Indiana school board candidates may declare a party (Senate Bill 287, 2025). Hanes and Stanley filed as Republicans; Sneed, Vetor and Davidson did not declare a party {ct_contested}{gc_cand}{hb_9cand}.

Elementary consolidation (April 2026): a Lancer Associates facility study presented Jan. 20, 2026 found structural problems at Summitville Elementary's 1938 gym section and offered two options: close Summitville and renovate Park Elementary ($23 million-$30 million) or build a new elementary and close both ($30 million-$36 million) {ct_facility}. On April 28 the board voted 6-1 to merge Summitville into Park Elementary in Fairmount, renamed Madison-Grant Elementary, starting in 2026-27; Bruce Stanley voted no {ct_consol}. Mann said the district was 'not in a financial hardship' and called it 'a stewardship of resources conversation'; he said no employee would lose a job {ct_consol}. A Summitville parent raised concerns about bus ride times and the loss of a community building {hb_summitville}.

Sixth grade move: on Dec. 9, 2025 the board voted 6-0 to move sixth graders to Madison-Grant Jr./Sr. High School starting in fall 2026 {ct_6th}. The new middle-school plan uses three 65-minute morning blocks for math, English and science/social studies, with special education staff joining those classes {ct_6th_plan}.

Budget and SEA 1: Mann told the board SEA 1 is projected to cost the district an average of $500,000 a year from its operations fund over the next five years {ct_kids}. In August 2025 the board heard a Policy Analytics presentation on SEA 1, which the district hired to provide monthly finance reports {ct_sea1}. On Sept. 29, 2026 the board adopted a 2027 budget advertised at $25,750,517, plus capital projects and bus replacement plans, 6-0 with Hanes absent {ct_budget27}. No operating or safety referendum is on the ballot for Madison-Grant; neighboring Mississinewa and Oak Hill have operating referendums {ct_contested}.

Library policy: on June 3, 2025 the board approved removing the novel 'We Are the Ants' from the junior/senior high library after a parent complaint and a staff committee review. At the July 22, 2025 meeting a resident criticized the decision as lacking transparency and asked the board to involve parents, community members and students in future book challenges {ct_book}.

Academics and career programs: the district reported that 27% of the Class of 2026 earned the Indiana College Core, 8% an associate degree and 50% an industry certification {ct_grad}. In 2025 the board received Indiana School Boards Association governance awards (Level 3 Distinguished for the board) {mg_min_20260414}.
Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or campaign website for any Madison-Grant candidate.
